item_arguments.argument: Define the local cubic basis and the value-and-slope formula on each strictly increasing interval.
Define a piecewise polynomial on each positive-width cell by Bernstein controls, with an explicit optional matching-control condition for continuity.
Evaluate basis values and derivatives at both endpoints using the power and chain rules, then reproduce the four monomials 1,t,t²,t³ directly to prove cubic reproduction.

Differentiate the Hermite formula using the power rule and express its derivative as a convex combination of the four corner quadratics on [0,3]²; use the real mean value theorem to pass derivative sign to monotonicity.
For finite strictly increasing nodes, define secants, interior weighted harmonic slopes, one-sided endpoint estimates with clip/cap branches, and the resulting Hermite pieces.

Prove every Bernstein weight is nonnegative (using the natural coefficient's zero/positive split), prove the weights sum to one by the binomial theorem, obtain finite control minima and maxima, then apply finite-product nonnegativity and finite-sum monotonicity cellwise.
Positive widths give nonzero endpoint denominators; on the harmonic branch both nonzero secants share a sign, so its weighted reciprocal sum cannot vanish.
Bound each interior harmonic slope relative to both neighboring secants and use the endpoint clip/cap formulas to obtain [0,3] ratios, including flat cells.

Use continuity, the intermediate value theorem, and the mean value theorem to fix the nonzero derivative sign and bound all secants; Taylor expansions and reciprocal cancellation give O(h²) interior slopes, and the one-sided endpoint estimate gives the same rate at both ends. Continuous f' and f''' are bounded on the compact interval.

Apply Hermite interpolation and C¹ matching, then the normalized-slope square on each nonflat cell; flat cells have equal values and zero endpoint slopes. Concatenate monotone cells for globally monotone data.

Bound f''' on the compact interval. Compare PCHIP with exact-slope Hermite: a degree-two Taylor residual gives O(h³) Hermite error for C³ data, while the O(h²) nodal slope errors contribute O(h³) through the h-scaled Hermite basis.
Expand the degree-two Bernstein controls (1/10,-2/5,1/10), evaluate p(0), p(1), and p(1/2), and verify positive samples do not guarantee interpolant positivity.

Verify the explicit three-piece natural cubic is C², interpolatory, and natural while its zero-data middle cell is negative; compute PCHIP's flat zero middle segment and apply the no-overshoot theorem.
Compute the secants, endpoint slopes, and two interior zero slopes, then apply the shape theorem to verify the exact flat cell and global monotonicity.
For f(x)=x² on five uniform nodes, compute the limited slope adjacent to zero, derive the Hermite-cell error h²t(1-t)²/2, and evaluate it at t=1/3.
